hypothesis: Keeping the authenticated request's own tool descriptions in the model presentation when switching to tool_choice=none may allow the final request to reuse earlier tokens without a speculative warmup. Real tool eligibility stays none. Both modes must be evaluated for emitted raw tool markup, unexpected calls, correctness and user-visible natural completion.
scope: Qwen2.5-7B, BF16, two isolated A100 40GB. Existing wide Riley profile, vLLM as a separate same-layout control. In each fresh service run the original short-history primer then history=200 with seed 761 and two newly chosen seeds 18081 and 19959. Each group has cold, immediate, delayed, reader and concurrent long-tool-result. Preserve both tool results, original 90-word user request and output cap. Log every attempted workflow, including failures. Tool IDs can differ across engines: compare actual prompt token hashes where available and stable logical inputs across arms.
gates: Compare each GPU separately. Require additional cached input on concurrent long-tool-result, no unexpected calls or textual tool markers on the final response, no loss of a previously passing workflow, and reduced long-tool-result natural completion on all three history-200 seeds before considering promotion. Flag any peer p95 content gap or completion regression above 5%. Compare candidate vs same-layout vLLM, using each group separately. Record actual citations, numbers, token and word counts, percentile explanation; mark interpretation requiring judgment. These synthetic groups cannot establish fleet SLOs.
